beats.t: Black hands poured from the fissure in the sky. The round skylight shattered, and hands fell into the reading room like rain.
Definitely worse than rain! Con artist, now would be a great time for a con!
Mr. Otter, take our lady's left. I'll eat the right.
Yundal removed his glove. The hole in his palm swirled and sucked in the three nearest black hands. Its rim widened by a fingernail's width.
Yundal, your hand! The hole's growing!
Right now, I'm more afraid of you getting smaller than it getting bigger.
Moka hurled an ember like a ball. One black hand recoiled from the burn. But the hands passed Yeoni by.
Huh? They're not coming for the pig.
Then who?
Yeoni stretched out a vine and caught the nearest hand. The instant it touched, the vine withered black. It wasn't holding the hand. It was being eaten.
They're eating my vine. Why are they so hungry?
They've been starving a long time. And today, they seem to have found something tastier than you, my lady.
The hands swarmed in only one direction. Toward the white cat by the window.
Yeoni, get down!
Yeongnyangi bristled all over. Golden blades rose from his paws and severed several black hands at once. But each cut hand split into two and lunged again.
Cat. You are a blade. A blade belongs in its sheath.
A black hand seized Yeongnyangi's rusted left paw. His knee buckled.
Let go. This isn't yours.
The hand did not release him. Black threads spread between its fingers and began winding tightly around his leg. The tips of his white fur turned gray.
Let go of his paw!
Something burst deep in Yeoni's chest. Fire like the noonday sun poured from their hoof. 丙 blazed red on the chart.
The flames burned the black hand. And did not stop. The fire that consumed the hand swept straight over the white paw in its grip.
Ghh.
The black hands scattered like screams. The sky's fissure slowly closed. Only the smells of burning and melting metal remained in the reading room.
Is it over? It's over, right? Pig, was that you? Hotter than the festival island's sun.
My lady, please turn down the fire. The books are sweating.
Yeoni looked at their own hooves. Embers still crackled at the tips. They hastily shook them out.
I've never done that much before. It was just... they grabbed Yeongnyangi's paw.
Then a low groan came from the window.
Yeongnyangi lay collapsed on the floor. The cloak covering his left paw had burned away, exposing everything he had hidden beneath.
Yeongnyangi.
Scorch marks spread from paw to shoulder. Red rust covered them. This was no wound from the last day or two.
How long has it been like this? This didn't happen today.
It's nothing.
Nothing spreads all the way to your shoulder?
Yeoni's hoof moved before an answer came. They drew out a thin vine and began wrapping his paw. As they wound it, the vine's tip touched the scorch marks and crumbled.
Stop. It won't help right now.
Stay still. I'll decide whether it helps.
My lady. Sit down. I'll explain.
You knew, too, Yundal?
Yes. Since the day Mr. Cat taught you the breathing exercise.
Moka, you too?
Since the festival island. The day you first shouted in the courtroom. Smoke came from the cat's paw.
When I asked him, he said he'd poison my skewers if I told the pig.
I never said that. I said I'd eat them all.
That's even crueler!
Since then? All those days, everyone but me?
Nobody answered. Moka lowered his tail, and Yundal put his gloved hand in his pocket. Their silence was the answer.
So I was the only one who didn't know. I was the only one happily going around making fire.
Your Month Stem is Byeong Fire. Hurting Officer. Fire that lets you say what you want and break free of constraints.
And Mr. Cat is Gyeong Metal, Direct Officer. The structure, the rules, the name tag.
When Hurting Officer meets Direct Officer, Direct Officer gets hurt. It's called Hurting Officer Meets Officer. The stronger your fire, the more Mr. Cat melts.
[ 丙 Hurting Officer → 庚 Direct Officer · Hurting Officer Meets Officer ]
丙 on the chart was still red-hot. Wherever its heat touched the corners of 庚, black scorch marks spread.
So. I did this? In the courtroom, at the noon concert, and now?
It isn't your fault. That's how the energies clash in this chart.
Then you should have told me that's how the chart works!
Why didn't you tell me?
Because you would put out your fire.
Of course I would! If my fire does this to you!
That's why I didn't say it. Without your fire, you aren't you. A festival that can't sing. Skewers with no taste. You saw them, too.
Then what about you? It's okay for you to melt?
That's why I'm by your side.
Don't say that. Saying things like that isn't cool at all.
Yeongnyangi fell silent. Yeoni rubbed their eyes with a hoof. Tears mixed with soot and smeared black.
With you, it's always later. You said you'd tell me when it was over. Is this when it's over? When the rust reaches your shoulder?
I'm sorry.
I'm not asking for an apology!
Then what do you want me to say?
I don't know! Just... just say it hurts when it hurts. Is that so hard?
The reading room went quiet. Moka stood frozen with the skewer plate, and Yundal's hand had stopped halfway through putting on his glove.
It hurts.
Huh?
It hurts. Every time you make fire. But if you can't make fire, that hurts more.
Yeoni could say nothing. Yeongnyangi slowly pushed himself up. His rusted paw dragged on the floor.
When I stay beside you, you become smaller. When you grow, I melt. That's our chart.
Then what are we supposed to do? One of us has to keep hurting?
No. One of us can step aside.
Yeongnyangi.
In that instant, words escaped Yeoni's mouth before thought could catch them. Like fire, with no time to stop them.
Then step aside! Don't stay next to me getting hurt! I'm not grateful for that at all!
Yeoni regretted it as soon as the words were out. But they had already fallen to the reading-room floor and rolled away.
Yes. That's right.
No, that's not...
Yeongnyangi turned away. His white tail vanished through the doorway. The door closed quietly. This time, there wasn't even a loud sound.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
庚 went dark on the chart. The blank was empty again. The vine around Yeoni's hoof drooped limply to the floor.
I told him to move aside. He really left.
Hey. Pig.
What?
Stop crying and go catch him. That's who you are. Talk first, run after.
At Mr. Cat's pace, he'll be at the bottom of the stairs about now. He can't go fast on that rusted paw.
What do I say when I catch him? Stay beside me, and he'll melt again.
We'll solve that together later. A chart is a problem, not a verdict. I've yet to see a problem without a way to solve it.
First time I'm trusting the con artist. Hurry!
Yeoni wiped their tears with a sleeve. Then they kicked open the door and ran.
As they raced downstairs, scenes flashed through Yeoni's mind. The cat who only nodded even after receiving one star. The back that stood before them in the courtroom.
His figure going alone to the river after the noon concert. His left paw walking strangely after the water. Yeoni had seen it all, and pretended not to see any of it.
(I knew, too. It wasn't just that nobody told me. I didn't ask.)
Outside the library lay a river. An empty ferryboat rocked on the current of starlight.
Yeongnyangi! Yeongnyangi, I said it wrong! Come back!
The call fell into the river and drifted away. The boat rocked once. Yeoni rushed over and looked inside. Empty.
What cat actually moves aside because you tell him to? Usually, you don't listen to a thing I say.
A single white hair lay on the boat's floor. Yeoni wound it around a hoof. Still warm.
There was no reply. Dots of red rust marked the river stones. The pawprints led downstream, then ended in the fog.
The mist was thick. Yeoni raised a hoof. Just a little fire would show the way.
An ember formed at the tip. Yeoni stared at it for a long time, then clenched their hoof and put it out.
If I light this fire, you'll hurt again somewhere.
Without fire, Yeoni walked into the mist. Feeling out each rust mark, they followed. Their hooves kept slipping on the cold stones.
Each time they fell, they checked the white hair first. Each time, it had grown a little colder.
I'll take back that one star. Give you five. So please answer me.
Only the water answered beyond the mist. The pawprints ended there.
Over the broken trail, a black shadow slowly crawled. A shadow shaped like a human hand.
No.
The shadow slipped into the fog and vanished. Along with the smell of rust.
